diagnostic_evidence.quote: We propose an explicit and an implicit exponentially weighted finite difference method.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper repeatedly describes scheme (eq:scheme) as explicit (abstract, Section 3.2, Theorem th:MFE). However the discretized mixed derivative term contains p^{n+1}_{j+1} and p^{n+1}_{j-1} (equivalently ν^n_{j±1} in the compact form), so each step requires solving a banded linear system in the unknowns (p^{n+1}_j)_j. The method is linearly implicit, not explicit; only the starting step (with ν^0=0) is explicit. This also explains why the derived stability region (τ ≤ ωεh for |β|<1) exceeds the domain-of-dependence bound of a genuinely explicit three-point-per-level stencil.

failure_location.quote: obtain an explicit symmetric two-step scheme as follows:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the weighted leapfrog method as linearly implicit (a banded linear solve per step) and note invertibility of the implicit operator; adjust the abstract and Section 3.2 wording.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit/implicit dichotomy is inaccurate; the 'explicit' method's per-step cost includes a linear solve. Error bounds and stability results are unaffected since the Fourier symbol e^{-iα}(1+iγ_θ) of the implicit part is uniformly invertible.
issues.title: Weighted leapfrog scheme is called explicit but couples p^{n+1}_{j±1} (linearly implicit)
issues.why_classification: The algorithm is well defined and all guarantees survive; only the characterization of its computational structure must be corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The $BC^1(\R)$-norm is stronger than the norm of the Wiener algebra $A(\R)$, as is implied by \eqref{eq:katz}.
    Hence, the $\mathcal{O}(\eps)$ defect bound is also valid in the $A(\R)$-norm.
The proof is based on \eqref{eq:katz} and follows the same steps as the proof in \cite[Lemma 4.2]{shi2025weighted}.
The remaining steps follow as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop}.

issues.failure_explanation: The second inequality in (eq:katz) is false: A(R) ⊂ C_0(R) by Riemann–Lebesgue, so e.g. f ≡ 1 has bounded f and f' but is not in A(R); the correct embedding is H^1(R) ⊂ A(R). Moreover, the defect d contains the factor e^{iκx/ε}, so ||d'||_∞ = O(1), not O(ε); even a correct BC^1-type embedding would not yield the claimed O(ε) A(R)-bound. The O(ε) bound in A(R) does hold, but only via modulation invariance of the A-norm together with an H^1 bound on the smooth profiles, which is not the argument given. The same flawed step is invoked in Proposition prop2 and in Lemma lem:defect-wiener.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (eq:katz) by ||f||_A ≤ C||f||_{H^1(R)}, use ||f e^{iκ·/ε}||_A = ||f||_A, and bound the (smooth, decaying) profile of the defect in H^1 uniformly in ε.
issues.overall_effect: The passage from maximum-norm to Wiener-algebra defect bounds in Propositions prop, prop2 and Lemma lem:defect-wiener is unsupported as written; all downstream results rely on these A(R) bounds.
issues.title: False Wiener-algebra embedding (eq:katz) used to transfer O(ε) defect bounds to the A(R)-norm
issues.why_classification: A standard, local replacement of the embedding argument restores every stated bound with no change in conclusions or rates.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop2 states u = (a + εb)e^{...} + O(ε^2), where b solves a linear Schrödinger equation forced by -2c_g ∂_t∂_ξ a and is generically nonzero for t>0. Dropping εb, as (eq:pq) does by defining p̃ = a^+ e^{...}, leaves an O(ε) remainder, not O(ε^2). The displayed O(ε^2) is therefore false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either replace O(ε^2) by O(ε) in (eq:pq), or include the εb^± correction terms in p̃ and q̃.
issues.overall_effect: Only the displayed claim (eq:pq) is wrong; (eq:upq), Algorithm alg and Theorems th:MFE/thm use only the O(ε) version, and Theorem thm:polarized correctly uses a+εb.
issues.title: (eq:pq) claims p = a^+ e^{...} + O(ε^2), but Proposition prop2 only gives O(ε) without the εb term
issues.why_classification: An isolated incorrect order statement with no downstream dependence; a one-line correction preserves all results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Comparing this expression with \eqref{eq:v-pola} then yields the second error bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The reconstructed velocity (eq:v-pola) contains ε c_g D_h p^n and ε^2 D_τ p^n, i.e. weighted difference quotients of the numerical solution. Writing p^n = p̃ + R^±, the contribution of the remainder to ε^2 v_+ is bounded only by ε||R||_∞/h + ε^2||R||_∞/τ. Theorem th:MFE gives only an L^∞ bound on R^±, so this is O(τ^2+h^2+ε) only when h ≳ ε and τ ≳ ε^2. In the regimes h ≪ ε or τ ≪ ε^2, which the theorem's ε-,τ-,h-independent constant explicitly covers, no bound on D_h R or D_τ R is established. The same gap affects the velocity bound of Theorem thm:polarized.

failure_location.quote: which, together with Theorem~\ref{th:MFE}, leads to the velocity error estimate in Theorem~\ref{thm}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a stability/consistency estimate for the error in a stronger norm controlling h^{-1}(e^{-iβ}e_{j+1}-e^{iβ}e_{j-1}) and τ^{-1}(e^{-iα}e^{n+1}-e^{iα}e^{n-1}) (e.g. via the eigen-decomposition in Fourier space, where the oscillatory-mode component of the error yields ε^2 D_τ e = O(||e||)), or restrict the velocity bounds to h ≥ cε, τ ≥ cε^2.
issues.overall_effect: The velocity error bounds in Theorems thm and thm:polarized are unproven uniformly in ε, τ, h; the solution error bounds are unaffected.
issues.title: Velocity error bounds require control of difference quotients of the numerical error, not provided by Theorem th:MFE
issues.why_classification: A contained additional stability argument in a stronger norm is needed; otherwise the velocity bounds lose the advertised uniformity in the classical regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: equivalent to the norm $\|\cdot\|_{A(\mathbb{R}) \times A(\mathbb{R})}$ uniformly in $\eps,\tau,h$ subject to \eqref{eq:stability}
where $C$ is independent of $\eps$, $\tau$, $h$, and $n$ with $t_n\le T$
Following the same procedure as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:stability} yields the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: At θh = β (mod 2π) one has γ̃_θ = 1 and γ_θ = α(1+κ^2) = αω^2, so γ̃_θ^2/(1+γ_θ^2) = 1/(1+α^2ω^4), which tends to 1 as α = τ/(ωε^2) → 0. The CFL condition (eq:stability) only bounds |α| from above, so no uniform μ<1 exists; ||V(θ)^{-1}||_2 ~ 1/|α| = ωε^2/τ and the claimed uniform equivalence of the norm |||·||| fails in the regime τ ≪ ε^2 (which the theorems explicitly include). The degeneracy is genuine: at this mode the recurrence reduces to leapfrog for ε^2 c_tt + 2iω c_t = 0, whose solution from (c^0,c^1) has amplitude ≈ |c^0| + (ε^2/τ)|c^1-c^0|, so the constant in Lemma lem:stability (for arbitrary p̃, hence arbitrary e^0, e^1) is not independent of ε and τ. The Crank–Nicolson lemma has the same defect (|γ_θ|^2 - 1 = ω^2τ^2/ε^4 → 0 at θh=β) and its proof defers to the same procedure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniform norm-equivalence argument by a θ-wise estimate: show 1+γ_θ^2-γ̃_θ^2 ≳ min(1,α^2) under (eq:stability) so that ||V^{-1}(ê^1,ê^0)|| ≲ |ê^0| + |ê^1-ê^0|/min(1,|α|), verify that the starting step gives ||e^1-e^0||_A ≲ min(τ,ε^2) (hence O(ε^2) after amplification), and note that the defect and nonlinearity enter with the compensating factor τ^2/(ε^2|1+iγ_θ|); alternatively restrict the results to τ ≥ cε^2.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform-in-(ε,τ,h) constants asserted in Lemmas th:stability, lem:stability-cn, lem:stability and hence in Theorems th:MFE, thm, thm:polarized are unsupported for τ ≪ ε^2; the theorems' claimed uniformity down to the classical regime rests on an invalid step.
issues.title: Norm equivalence in linear stability is not uniform: eigenvalues coalesce as α = τ/(ωε^2) → 0
issues.why_classification: The theorems are likely true but require a new, contained stability argument exploiting the specific initial error; the simple alternative of restricting to τ ≥ cε^2 would exclude an advertised regime.
